bunt. Quid est τὸ μὴ αἴτιον ὡς αἴτιον ponere, nisi hoc est?

tiaq; animi abreptos principes reprehenderat, ad bo-
nos orationem habet, & omneis ad bonum reuocat,
monitis piis & salutaribus. Falsa igitur consequentia.

page.notes: The Greek line at the start of the sixth line of the block is badly damaged and is marked illegible. The Greek phrase after "est" is only partly certain. The right edge shows cut-off fragments of the neighbouring page's notes, left out as not belonging to this page. Two words in the line "Iabefactare" appear to be a run-on from "labefactare" and are printed as seen.
